messages.name: Priya Shah
messages.subject: Team seats for 6 narrators
messages.message: We record e-learning modules with six freelance narrators. Can we share one Pro plan, or do we need a plan each? We'd also like the exported error reports in our LMS.

messages.name: Mara Quinn
messages.subject: Accents and regional spellings
messages.message: I narrate in British English. Does SoundProof flag 'colour' vs 'color' as an error when the script uses British spelling?
messages.admin_reply: No: British and American spellings count as the same word, so 'colour' read from a script that says 'color' is marked correct.

messages.name: Tobias Reid
messages.subject: Numbers in scripts
messages.message: My scripts write numbers as digits (12, 2026) and I read them as words. Will that count against my accuracy?
messages.admin_reply: Numbers are compared the way they are read aloud, so '12' in the script and 'twelve' in the recording match. A wrong number still shows up as an error.

messages.name: Hana Sato
messages.subject: Pausing my subscription
messages.message: I'm between audiobook contracts for two months. Can I pause rather than cancel and keep my history?

feedback.text: We used to proof every chapter twice by ear. Now the first pass takes minutes and the proofer only checks what SoundProof flags.
It caught a wrong weight limit in a safety module before it went to 400 warehouse staff. That alone paid for the year.
Click-to-seek on every flagged word is the feature I didn't know I needed. Pickups are so much faster.
Comparing two takes side by side made choosing the keeper easy.
Works well, but I'd love support for scripts with stage directions in brackets.

samples.title: The Lighthouse Keeper, Chapter 3 (take 1)
samples.script: Chapter Three. The storm arrived an hour before midnight, exactly as the old almanac had promised. Margaret climbed the ninety-two steps of the lighthouse with a lantern in one hand and her father's brass key in the other. At the top, the great lens was already turning, throwing its pale beam across a sea the colour of slate. She checked the oil, wound the clockwork, and wrote the time in the logbook in small, careful letters. Far below, the fishing boats were running for the harbour, their lights rising and falling like sparks above a fire. One of them was late. Margaret counted the boats twice, then a third time, and each time the answer was the same: eleven, not twelve. She pressed her hand against the cold glass and waited for the twelfth light to appear.

samples.title: Q3 product update video
samples.script: Welcome to the third-quarter product update. This quarter we shipped the three features customers asked for most. First, offline mode now syncs automatically when you reconnect, with no manual export. Second, shared workspaces support up to fifty collaborators, up from twenty. Third, the new reporting dashboard loads in under two seconds, even for accounts with a million records. Support tickets about slow reports fell by forty-one percent in the first month. Next quarter, we will focus on single sign-on, audit logs and a redesigned mobile app. Thank you for building with us.

samples.title: Warehouse safety briefing, Module 2
samples.script: Module two: safe lifting. Before you lift any load, check its weight on the label and test it by tipping one corner. Never lift more than twenty-five kilograms on your own. Stand close to the load with your feet shoulder-width apart, bend your knees, and keep your back straight. Hold the load close to your waist and lift smoothly, without jerking or twisting. If you need to turn, move your feet instead of your body. When a load is too heavy or awkward, use a trolley or ask a colleague for help. Report any strain or injury to your supervisor on the same day.
